subject: general
question: In which Indian state do 'Ahars', a type of water harvesting system, exist?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **South Bihar's Ahar pynes,** which are regionally **endemic floodwater gathering systems, **have historically been the **main source of irrigation in this area.**
 
• **Ahars, reservoirs with embankments on three sides, are constructed at the termini of natural drainage systems like rivulets or man-made structures like Pynes.**
 
• **Pynes are rivers' diversion canals that are led off for irrigation and water storage in Ahars.**
 
• When compared to North Bihar, this area receives very little rainfall, hence it is primarily to their credit that paddy agriculture has been made practicable there.
 
• **The district of Gaya was where the system reached its pinnacle of development.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Rainwater harvesting**

 
 
• **Technology that collects and stores rainwater for human use is known as a rainwater harvesting system**, also known as a **rainwater collecting system **or a **rainwater catchment system.**
 
• Rainwater collection systems can be as basic as buckets or as complex as buildings with** pumps, tanks, and purification systems.**
 
• The **nonpotable water can be filtered for use as drinking water** and utilized to** irrigate lawns, wash automobiles, wash clothes, and flush toilets.**
 
• In affluent nations, rainwater collection is frequently used to augment the primary supply of water during times of **regional water shortages.**
 
• When a drought strikes, it supplies water, can lessen flooding in low-lying areas, and lessens the need for wells, which might allow groundwater levels to be sustained.
 
• **By increasing the number of dried borewells and wells, rainwater collection increases the amount of water that is available during dry seasons.**
